source: Prek Leap National School of Agriculture - "Banana Varieties Giving High Yield and Good Taste Quality" (ពូជចេកផ្តល់ទិន្នផលខ្ពស់ និងគុណភាពសជាតិ) variety trial report, January 2007
text:
The trial's own conclusion section reports that, of the 26 accessions planted, 6 had not yet produced fruit by the end of the data-collection period (26 June 2006, about 10 months after the 26 August 2005 planting date); the remaining 20 accessions (about 77% of those tested) did flower and fruit within the trial period.

Among the varieties that fruited, the full cycle from planting to fruit maturity ranged from as short as 161 days for the fastest accession up to 394 days for the slowest. The report notes that 17 of the imported ITC accessions (about 74% of the imported set) grew, flowered, fruited and could be successfully propagated further under Prek Leap's growing conditions, supporting their suitability for further evaluation as potential new Cambodian banana varieties.
